headline: Green claims ban begins as Machinery and EUDR updates emerge
summary: The EU's Empowering Consumers directive has begun applying, restricting generic environmental claims on consumer tools and batteries. Technical updates were also published for the Machinery Regulation and upcoming EUDR enforcement. Sustainability teams should review product marketing and verify whether garden tools contain regulated wood.

items.title: EU anti-greenwashing rules enter into application
items.what: The Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition rules have begun applying, banning generic environmental claims, unverified sustainability labels, and unsubstantiated climate-neutrality claims.
items.meaning: As an EU consumer brand, all environmental statements on power tools, packaging, and battery platforms now require recognized certification or demonstrable substantiation.
items.action: Audit consumer packaging, manuals, and marketing copy to remove generic green claims lacking robust verification.

items.title: Corrigendum published for Machinery Regulation implementation rules
items.what: The EU published a corrigendum amending Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 regarding the implementation of harmonised rules under the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230.
items.meaning: Power tools and garden equipment technical files must align with the updated Machinery framework before it replaces the Machinery Directive on 20 January 2027.
items.action: Confirm that engineering leads and Chinese OEMs have incorporated the latest Machinery Regulation specifications into product roadmaps.

items.title: Commission updates EUDR customs codes and IT guidance
items.what: The EU issued updated customs codes and Information System guidance ahead of the deforestation regulation's scheduled 30 December 2026 application date.
items.meaning: If any garden tools incorporate regulated timber parts, such as wooden handles, imports will require full supply-chain geolocation data and due diligence filings.
items.action: Screen bills of materials for timber components to determine if any product lines require EUDR supplier due diligence.
